body.zh: 一位中国网络安全专家向德国之声透露了中国新型高科技警务的细节。从滑雪场面部识别到火车座位，该系统可以跟踪任何人并编制“整体档案”。 当一位化名 NetAskari 的网络安全研究人员最近点击一个不安全的中文网络仪表板上标有“查询记者档案”的选项卡时，他预计会看到一堆自动生成的模拟数据。 取而代之的是，熟悉的面孔出现在屏幕上。这是 2021 年左右驻扎在中国首都北京的几乎所有外国记者的综合数据库，包括在出入境管理局拍摄的官方护照照片、私人手机号码、签证详细信息和出生日期。他还发现自己的确切个人信息隐藏在中国警方的监视名单上。 “这比令人震惊更有趣，”内特阿斯卡里告诉德国之声。 “当你在中国担任记者时，你基本上会认为你总是在他们的监视范围内。但令我惊讶的是访问这个高度敏感的系统是多么容易。” NetAskari 偶然发现的是现代中国新兴的“全息轮廓”系统的一部分。 他无意中访问了为主办 2022 年冬季奥运会的河北省张家口市公安局设计的远程跟踪系统演示版本。 虽然它只是一个测试面板，但它填充了真实的数据集，清楚地概述了中国国家监控机器的轨迹，该机器正在从简单的街道摄像头网络迅速演变为数据融合的、24/7、预测性的社会控制庞然大物。 多年来，中国运营着世界上最广泛的闭路电视网络。一项名为“雪亮”（明亮的眼睛）项目的大规模倡议旨在合并这些分布在全国各地的监视孤岛。 但张家口警方仪表板上的数据显示了当局可以追踪个人的详细信息。 该系统不再仅仅依赖街角的警察摄像头。它准确记录目标从北京或上海到达时所占用的具体火车车厢和座位号。 它甚至将当地滑雪场的面部识别检票口拍摄的照片直接同步到其跟踪机制中。研究人员最近在张家口滑雪的熟人的动作被精确标记，并在系统中绘制出详细的轨迹。 研究人员指出：“这个想法只是实时处理来自尽可能多的传感器的尽可能多的数据。” 该系统记录日常行为，例如汽油消耗、常规购物地点以及个人是否经常访问“请愿区”。 这项大规模的数据融合工作试图……

reflection.en: The news of pervasive surveillance systems highlights the immense power states can wield over individuals. When such power is unchecked, it can feel like living under constant scrutiny, eroding personal freedom and privacy. This reminds us of the biblical warning about rulers who oppress their people, creating an environment of fear rather than security.
reflection.zh: 普遍存在的监控系统新闻突显了国家对个人可能施加的巨大权力。当这种权力不受制约时，人们可能会感到生活在持续的审视之下，个人自由和隐私受到侵蚀。这提醒我们圣经中关于压迫人民、制造恐惧而非安全的统治者的警告。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Taiwan: Trump prods China with offer of direct Taipei talks
title.zh: 台湾：特朗普提议与台北直接对话，以此刺激中国

summary.en: Donald Trump has indicated he would engage in direct talks with Taiwan's president regarding the purchase of US arms. This action would deviate from established diplomatic norms of over four decades and is expected to be perceived as a challenge by China.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将与台湾领导人就购买美国武器进行直接对话。此举将打破四十多年的外交惯例，并可能被中国视为一种冒犯。

body.en:
Donald Trump has said he will talk with Taiwan's president about purchasing US arms. The move would break over four decades of protocol and be an affront to China.

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday reiterated his intention to hold direct talks with Taiwan 's President Lai Ching-te over a reported $14 billion (€12 billion) arms deal — the first direct talks between the presidents of both countries in over four decades.

"I'll speak to him. I speak to everybody," said Trump when asked about the situation.

Taiwan's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday that Lai would be "happy to discuss these matters with President Trump."

It added that Lai is "committed to maintaining the stable status quo in the Taiwan Strait."

Trump's statement was the second such made since his state visit to China last week.

The US leader previously said he had "a great meeting" with Chinese President Xi Jinping , adding, "We'll work on that… the Taiwan problem."

The US officially shifted Taiwanese diplomatic recognition from Taipei (the Republic of China, or ROC) to Beijing (the People's Republic of China, or PRC) in 1979 as part of its "One China" policy of strategic ambiguity and has not engaged in public presidential communications with Taiwanese leaders since that time.

That same year, the US also established the Taiwan Relations Act, committing itself by law to providing Taiwan with the means to defend itself against regional threats.

Although the US has continued to engage in backchannel talks with Taiwan, public displays of support from Washington are frowned upon by Beijing, which considers the self-governing democracy part of its territory and has threatened to take the island republic by force if necessary.

During Trump's recent state visit, China's Xi made clear that the handling of the Taiwan issue would be key to maintaining stability in US-China relations, warning that missteps could lead to an "extremely dangerous situation."

Trump has suggested US arms sales could be used as a bargaining chip with Beijing on the issue.

A spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry urged Trump to "handle the Taiwan issue with extreme caution and stop sending wrong signals to the separatist forces of Taiwan independence."

Taiwan is heavily reliant on US arms to deter China and is eager to double down on the $11 billion deal approved by the Trump administration in December.
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将与台湾总统讨论购买美国武器的问题。此举将打破四十多年来的协议，是对中国的侮辱。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周三重申，他打算与台湾总统赖清德就一项据报道价值 140 亿美元（120 亿欧元）的军火交易进行直接会谈，这是四十多年来两国总统之间的首次直接会谈。 当被问及情况时，特朗普说：“我会和他说话。我会和每个人说话。” 台湾外交部周四表示，赖清德将“很乐意与特朗普总统讨论这些问题”。 声明补充说，黎智英“致力于维持台湾海峡的稳定现状”。 这是特朗普自上周对中国进行国事访问以来第二次发表此类声明。 这位美国领导人此前曾表示，他与中国国家主席习近平进行了“一次精彩的会面”，并补充道，“我们将致力于解决台湾问题。” 作为其“一个中国”战略模糊政策的一部分，美国于 1979 年正式将与台湾的外交承认从台北（中华民国，简称 ROC）转向北京（中华人民共和国，简称中华人民共和国），并且从那时起就没有与台湾领导人进行公开的总统沟通。 同年，美国还制定了《与台湾关系法》，依法承诺为台湾提供防御地区威胁的手段。 尽管美国继续与台湾进行秘密谈判，但北京方面对华盛顿公开表示支持表示不满，北京认为自治民主是其领土的一部分，并威胁在必要时以武力占领这个岛国。 在特朗普最近的国事访问期间，中国国家主席习近平明确表示，处理台湾问题是维护美中关系稳定的关键，并警告说，失误可能导致“极其危险的局面”。 特朗普表示，美国的军售可以作为在这个问题上与北京讨价还价的筹码。 中国外交部发言人敦促特朗普“高度谨慎处理台湾问题，停止向台独分裂势力发出错误信号”。 台湾严重依赖美国武器来威慑中国，并渴望加倍落实特朗普政府去年 12 月批准的 110 亿美元协议。

reflection.en: International relations often involve navigating complex protocols and sensitivities to maintain stability. The biblical call to "live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on you," reminds leaders and nations of the ongoing responsibility to seek harmonious coexistence. Even when pursuing national interests, wisdom suggests considering the broader...
reflection.zh: 国际关系常需在复杂的礼仪和敏感性中航行，以维持稳定。圣经呼吁“若是可能，总要尽力与众人和睦”，提醒领导人和国家有责任持续寻求和谐共存。即使在追求国家利益时，智慧也建议要考虑对全球和平与外交理解的更广泛影响。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: 'My dear friend': Putin and Xi praise partnership during talks in Beijing
title.zh: “我的挚友”：普京和习近平在北京会谈中赞扬伙伴关系

summary.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping praised their partnership during talks in Beijing. China continues to be a significant and loyal economic partner to Russia, despite international economic and financial sanctions imposed on Russia by other countries.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯总统普京和中国国家主席习近平在北京会谈期间赞扬了两国伙伴关系。尽管其他国家对俄罗斯实施了经济和金融制裁，中国仍然是俄罗斯重要而忠诚的经济伙伴。

body.en:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has lauded his close ties with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, saying the nations are partners in trade and international affairs during bilateral talks in Beijing.

Xi welcomed Putin with a ceremony at the Great Hall of the People only days after meeting United States President Donald Trump.

The quick succession of Trump's and Putin's visits highlighted China's growing role as an international superpower, experts say.

Putin greeted Xi warmly as they met for the bilateral talks, describing the Chinese president as a "dear friend".

"We are truly delighted to see you. We keep in constant touch, both personally and through our aides in the government," he said.

Xi also stressed the "political mutual trust and strategic co-operation" between the countries, according to Chinese state media.

The two leaders have praised each other profusely in the past — Xi once describing Putin as his "best and most intimate friend".

Xi and Putin were set to focus on energy and security as well as their overall ties.

Chinese state media reported both parties agreed to extend a friendship treaty first signed in 2001.

China became Russia's top trading partner after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

China has said it is neutral in the conflict, maintaining trade ties with Russia despite economic and financial sanctions against Russia by the US and Europe.

China is the top customer for Russian oil and gas supplies, and Russia expects the war in Iran to increase the demand.

"The driving force behind economic co-operation is Russian-Chinese collaboration in the energy sector," Putin said.

"Amid the crisis in the Middle East, Russia continues to maintain its role as a reliable supplier of resources, while China remains a responsible consumer of these resources."

Xi stressed the need for the "complete cessation of hostilities" in the Middle East, according to Chinese state media.

"An early end to the conflict will help reduce disruptions to energy supply stability, the smooth flow of industrial and supply chains, and international trade order," Xi said.

A Russian presidential aide said earlier that Russia's oil exports to China grew by 35 per cent in the first quarter of 2026. Russia was also one of the biggest exporters of natural gas to China.

Putin said China and Russia's co-operation in foreign policy is "one of the key stabilising factors on the international stage".

In February 2022, just weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine, China and Russia announced a "no limits" partnership during a trip by Putin to Beijing.

Despite taking a neutral stance in the conflict, China supports Russia through frequent state visits, growing trade and joint military drills.

title.en: Melbourne teenager becomes youngest Australian to summit Mount Everest
title.zh: 墨尔本少年成为最年轻的澳大利亚珠穆朗玛峰登顶者

summary.en: The 18-year-old's singular achievement comes as the number of climbers ascending to the world's tallest peak hits a record high.
summary.zh: 这位18岁少年独特的成就，正值登顶世界最高峰的登山者人数创下历史新高之际。

body.en:
An 18-year-old from Melbourne has become the youngest Australian to summit Mount Everest, reaching the peak of the world's tallest mountain on her second attempt.

Bianca Adler completed the ascent of the 8,849-metre summit alongside two Nepali guides, surpassing the previous Australian record holders Alyssa Azar and Gabby Kanizay.

Her ascent comes as the daily number of climbers summiting Everest from the Nepal side hits a record high of 274. Concerns over overcrowding, congestion in the 'death zone' at the top of the world's tallest mountain and threats to climber safety have been going on for years.

Speaking to SBS Nepali after returning to Kathmandu, Adler described the physical exhaustion of the climb and the relief of finally turning back down the mountain.

"It's a mix of emotions because it feels amazing to reach the top and on the other hand, just to stop going up because it is quite tiring," she said.

"It's really exhausting being at those altitudes because there is a really little amount of oxygen."

Adler said the descent was among the toughest parts of the expedition, after completing a gruelling 23-hour push from Camp Four to the summit and back to Camp Two.

"We arrived at base camp in the morning, ate a little bit and then had to pack up all our gear that we had spread out over the past few months," she said.

Despite the physical strain, Adler said her previous mountaineering experience helped her body adapt to the extreme conditions.

"With experience on other mountains, my body has sort of learned how to adapt a little bit better to those higher altitudes and how to function better on less food and water."

Adler spent about 20 minutes at the summit, reaching the top around 2:20am local time.

"It's a really amazing moment knowing you have reached the top of the world," she said.

"But we also have to go down and we are only halfway at the top and most of the accidents happen on the way down, so you also have to stay focused."

She said overcrowding near the summit meant climbers had to briefly wait their turn at the peak.

"We were the second group at the summit that day so you need to let everyone have their moment at the top of the world," she said.

"We also have to be super mindful not to take our big gloves off for too long because that is how you get frostbite."

Adler praised fellow Australian climbers Alyssa Azar and Gabby Kanizay, and said they had inspired her own mountaineering ambitions.

"Ever since a few years ago when I was training for other mountains, I had just looked up to those women," she said.

body.zh: 一名来自墨尔本的 18 岁女孩成为登顶珠穆朗玛峰最年轻的澳大利亚人，这是她第二次尝试登顶世界最高峰。 比安卡·阿德勒 (Bianca Adler) 与两名尼泊尔向导一起完成了 8,849 米顶峰的登顶，超越了之前的澳大利亚纪录保持者阿丽莎·阿扎 (Alyssa Azar) 和加比·卡尼泽 (Gabby Kanizay)。 她的登顶正值每日从尼泊尔一侧登顶珠穆朗玛峰的登山者人数达到创纪录的274人之际。多年来，人们对这座世界最高峰“死亡区”过度拥挤、拥堵以及登山者安全受到威胁的担忧一直存在。 回到加德满都后，阿德勒在接受 SBS 尼泊尔语采访时描述了攀登过程中的体力消耗以及最终返回下山时的轻松感。 “这是一种复杂的情绪，因为到达顶峰的感觉很棒，但另一方面，只是停止上升，因为它很累，”她说。 “在这些海拔高度真的很累，因为氧气含量非常少。” 阿德勒表示，在完成了从四号营地到顶峰再返回二号营地长达 23 小时的艰苦跋涉后，下撤是此次探险中最艰难的部分之一。 “我们早上到达大本营，吃了一点东西，然后不得不收拾好过去几个月我们分散的所有装备，”她说。 尽管身体紧张，阿德勒说她之前的登山经历帮助她的身体适应了极端条件。 “凭借在其他山上的经验，我的身体已经学会了如何更好地适应那些更高的海拔，以及如何在更少的食物和水的情况下更好地发挥作用。” 阿德勒在山顶花了大约 20 分钟，于当地时间凌晨 2 点 20 分左右到达山顶。 “知道自己已经到达世界之巅，这真是一个令人惊奇的时刻，”她说。 “但我们也必须往下走，我们才到了山顶的一半，大多数事故都发生在下山的路上，所以你也必须保持专注。” 她说，山顶附近人满为患，意味着登山者必须在山顶短暂等待。 “我们是那天登顶的第二组，所以你需要让每个人都在世界之巅享受属于自己的时刻，”她说。 “我们还必须非常小心，不要长时间脱下大手套，因为这就是冻伤的原因。” 阿德勒赞扬了澳大利亚登山者阿莉莎·阿扎尔和加比·卡尼泽，并表示他们激发了她自己的登山雄心。 “自从几年前我在其他山峰训练时，我就一直尊敬那些女性，”她说。 据当地官员称，周三，274 名登山者从尼泊尔一侧登顶，再次引发了人们对珠穆朗玛峰所谓“死亡区”拥堵的担忧。 “死亡地带”是指高海拔地区...

reflection.en: The ascent of Mount Everest demands immense discipline, training, and perseverance, much like an athlete striving for a perishable crown. This remarkable feat reminds us of the human spirit's capacity to push limits. Yet, it also invites us to consider what "crown" we are ultimately striving for, and whether it is one that will last eternally.

title.zh: 澳大利亚经典车改装电动车：昂贵趋势的背后

summary.en: A niche group of classic car owners in Australia is converting their used vehicles to electric power, giving them a modern "second life." This trend is noted for its high cost, prompting questions about its overall value.

body.en:
In a suburban garage in Sydney, Dr Adrian Cohen is polishing his pride and joy — a restored cross-country wagon now running silently on electric power.

A vehicle once built for war in Germany has found an unlikely second life in the clean-energy transition.

"When it was in military service, it was known as the wolf. It was designed to take the tough stuff."

title.en: The biggest budget myths: why claims of ‘massive tax bills’ and an investor exodus fall short

body.en:
The budget announced some of the most consequential tax reform measures in a decades.

Among them were changes to the capital gains tax – the tax you pay on the profit from the sale of an investment.

The budget measures are yet to be legislated – they may well look different by the time they pass parliament.

Investors in new home builds can choose whether to stick with the old 50% discount or go with the new inflation-linked approach (they can also keep negative gearing).

The budget also included a 30% minimum tax on the after-inflation capital gains, with an exception for people on income support payments, like the age pension or jobseeker.

If you hold an asset before that date, your eventual capital gains on the investment will get the 50% discount up to 30 June 2027, and profits after will be taxed under the inflation-linked regime.

Whether you pay more or less than the current 50% CGT discount – on any asset – depends primarily on the relative rates of inflation and return over the holding period.

For example, if after one year your shares went up 5% in value and inflation was 2.5%, then you will pay tax on half of the capital gain. Sound familiar? That’s the same as the existing 50% discount.

But say you instead earned 10%. Then your discount would only be 25% (the 2.5% inflation as a share of the 10% return).

In contrast, if you earn 4% and sell after one year, you only pay tax on the 1.5% real gain. In this case your CGT discount is 62.5%.

As mentioned, the capital gains made before mid-2027 on existing investments held on budget day will still get the 50% discount, while the returns made after that date will get the inflation-adjusted capital gains discount.

That changes the simple equation from above, as it depends how long you held the assets under one regime versus the other.

Andrew Lilley, an economist at investment bank Barrenjoey, helpfully crunched some numbers .

If you bought in 2023, made 10% a year, and sold in 2030, he calculates 55% of your capital gains will be taxable.

Any business with annual turnover below $2m, or below $6m in assets, will remain eligible for CGT concessions.

The treasurer’s office has highlighted tax data showing that nine out of ten small businesses get these concessions, “meaning they can pay reduced or zero CGT when they sell their business”.

But many small business owners hope to one day be a big business-owner. For them, they may well end up paying more tax on the eventual sale of their business.

There is an issue for entrepreneurs who start their business on a shoestring – a laptop and hours and hours of work. The initial cost base is close to zero, so how do you account for inflation on a zero base?

body.en:
Australia's jobs market is starting to soften, with the latest unemployment figures strengthening expectations the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) could hold interest rates steady next month.

Meanwhile, the fallout from the federal budget continues, with proposed tax changes prompting fresh debate around wealth planning and investment structures — including testamentary discretionary trusts.

And investors are increasingly turning their attention to space, as the sector emerges as one of the market's newest — and riskiest — frontiers.

The unemployment rate climbed to 4.5 per cent in April, the highest level since late 2021, with nearly 19,000 jobs lost during the month. Women accounted for much of the decline, while youth unemployment also increased.

The labour market remains relatively resilient. But historically, economists say, the rise suggests higher interest rates and global uncertainty are beginning to bite.

Businesses are also becoming more cautious. Slower consumer spending, higher borrowing costs and rising input prices are all weighing on confidence.

It means the RBA is likely to hold off on lifting interest rates at its next meeting in June — but inflation remains a problem .

The federal budget's proposed tax overhaul continued to dominate financial conversations this week, particularly around capital gains tax (CGT) and family wealth structures.

On Friday, the government signalled it was open to discussing its proposed changes to discretionary testamentary trusts.

A testamentary trust is created through a will, but only comes into effect after the person dies.

In its most basic form, it can hold investments such as property, shares, and cash to help preserve the assets.

The income they produce can then be distributed to chosen family members and adjusted every year — even to children who are taxed at adult rates.

This can effectively lower the total tax paid by a family over many years if the income falls into lower tax brackets.

The proposed budget changes, however, attract a 30 per cent minimum tax instead.

Meanwhile, many small businesses and start-up operators are concerned that the proposed CGT changes will stifle innovation.

The global space economy moved further into the spotlight this week after Elon Musk opened the books on space exploration company SpaceX ahead of its expected share market debut.

The company lost nearly US$5 billion ($7 billion) last year, despite generating around US$18 billion ($25.2 billion) in revenue. Yet investors are still expected to value the business at an extraordinary US$1.75 trillion ($2.45 trillion).

title.en: The two best places to invest your money in Australia after 'major' budget shake-up

summary.en: Significant changes to tax discounts in the 2026 federal budget are likely to shift how and where people choose to invest.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Changes to the capital gains discount and negative gearing are likely to change how Australians invest their money, experts say.

The Albanese government unveiled ambitious tax reforms as part of the budget released this month , sparking debate on how Australians should be taxed.

The changes include replacing the 50 per cent capital gains tax (CGT) discount from 1 July next year and limiting negative gearing on properties purchased after 12 May to new builds.

Jeff Coulton, associate professor in accounting at the University of New South Wales' Business School, says he believes the changes will trigger a "structural reallocation" of capital.

Coulton believes property investment will likely shift towards newly built homes, and share market investors will favour companies in Australia that pay dividends.

He notes the budget measures have not yet been legislated and are subject to negotiation before being finalised.

"But assuming the announced budget measures are reflected in the final enacted law, I think it would be a relatively major change in investor behaviour because it does dramatically change the relative attractiveness of certain types of investments."

There are two ways investors generally make money from shares: gaining a share of the profits (dividend income) or selling their stock for more than they paid (capital gains).

Coulton says the CGT changes make selling stock less attractive and this will impact riskier investments in businesses, such as start-ups, the most because they are more likely to invest profits back into their operations rather than pay shareholders a dividend.

"Early-stage investors will typically be looking for a capital return rather than a dividend return, and the proposed changes have made a capital return relatively less attractive," he says.

Instead, money may be shifted to shares in established companies, such as the major banks and mature mining and industrial companies, because they are more likely to pay dividends to shareholders.

Preference could also be given to companies that pay tax in Australia because they receive franking (or imputation) credits that investors can use to reduce the tax they pay on dividends.

"This budget didn't do anything to alter this dividend imputation system, but what it did do is it made franked dividends relatively more attractive because the capital gain side has become less concessional," Coulton says.

But he says young people are often better off investing in riskier companies that don't pay dividends, because they have more time to ride the ups and downs of the share market, and riskier investments generally deliver higher long-term returns.

title.en: 'Like a sneeze': Race to build Australian AI data centres generates concern
title.zh: “就像打喷嚏一样”：竞相建设澳大利亚人工智能数据中心引发担忧

summary.en: Tech companies are racing to build AI data centres, but there's a major question of where they should be built.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Community and environmental groups have joined the call to suspend data centre approvals in Australia while authorities determine the true impact of the artificial intelligence hubs.

Sydney Water also repeated its warning data centres could use up to one quarter of the city's drinking water within a decade, and infrastructure investment would need to rise to meet demand.

The warnings came on Friday at the third hearing of the NSW government's data centre inquiry, which heard from organisations including energy providers, local councils and business groups.

Australia has become the second-largest destination for data centre investments worldwide as tech companies attempt to meet demand for AI tools.

But questions remain over their electricity and water consumption, Carbon Zero Initiative strategy lead Alexander Hoysted said, and energy providers have had little chance to assess their impact.

"It's a little bit like a sneeze — it starts slowly and then all of a sudden these issues burst onto the scene very quickly," he said.

Despite claims data centres' water consumption had been exaggerated, Sydney Water managing director Darren Cleary repeated the organisation's forecast that data centres could use up to 25 per cent of the city's drinkable water by 2035.

"Our forecasts do reflect applications that are coming in that are planning to go ahead and there's clearly uncertainty when we get towards that 10-year time frame," he said.

"We have a large new industry developing in west or in greater Sydney that will add a significant new demand to our system."

Data centres' commitments to renewable energy should also be examined closely, Greenpeace Australia Pacific campaigner Solaye Snider said, and a moratorium should be placed on approvals until the industry has greater certainty.

"We need to pause, especially on the largest and most energy-intensive proposals right now, because we simply don't have enough renewable energy readily available," she said.

"We also want to scrutinise some of the claims that are being made by data centre operators and the data centre lobby around this."

The Lane Cove Responsible Planning Group also called for a moratorium, with member Paul Trainor telling the inquiry planning regulations were inadequate.

Six data centres were planned for the Sydney suburb, he said, including one within 20 metres of homes and 160m of a school, despite concerns about noise and air pollution.

"If data centres are truly critical infrastructure, they must be planned to a far higher standard and not cluster beside homes, beside schools, beside recreation areas without enforceable statewide planning rules and cumulative impact assessments," he said.

body.zh: 社区和环保组织已加入呼吁，暂停澳大利亚数据中心的审批，同时当局正在确定人工智能中心的真正影响。 悉尼水务局还重申其警告，数据中心可能会在十年内消耗该市四分之一的饮用水，并且需要增加基础设施投资才能满足需求。 这些警告是在周五新南威尔士州政府数据中心调查的第三次听证会上发出的，能源提供商、地方议会和商业团体等组织都在听证会上发出了这些警告。 随着科技公司试图满足人工智能工具的需求，澳大利亚已成为全球第二大数据中心投资目的地。 但零碳倡议战略负责人亚历山大·霍伊斯特德表示，电力和水的消耗仍然存在问题，能源供应商几乎没有机会评估其影响。 “这有点像打喷嚏——开始得很慢，然后突然这些问题很快就出现了，”他说。 尽管声称数据中心的耗水量被夸大，但悉尼水务公司总经理达伦·克利里 (Darren Cleary) 重申了该组织的预测，即到 2035 年，数据中心的用水量将占该市饮用水的 25%。 他说：“我们的预测确实反映了计划继续进行的申请，但当我们达到 10 年的时间框架时，显然存在不确定性。” “我们在西部或大悉尼正在发展一个大型新产业，这将为我们的系统增加大量新需求。” 澳大利亚太平洋绿色和平组织活动人士索莱·斯奈德表示，还应仔细审查数据中心对可再生能源的承诺，并应暂停批准，直到该行业获得更大的确定性。 她说：“我们需要暂停，特别是在目前规模最大、能源最密集的提案上，因为我们根本没有足够的可再生能源。” “我们还想仔细审查数据中心运营商和数据中心游说团体就此提出的一些主张。” Lane Cove 责任规划小组也呼吁暂停，成员 Paul Trainor 表示调查规划规定不够充分。 他表示，尽管担心噪音和空气污染，但仍计划在悉尼郊区建设六个数据中心，其中一个距离住宅 20 米以内，距离学校 160 m 以内。 他说：“如果数据中心确实是关键基础设施，那么它们必须按照更高的标准进行规划，而不是在没有可执行的全州规划规则和累积影响评估的情况下聚集在家庭、学校、娱乐区旁边。” 新法规应该解决他们对用水、住房和成本的担忧……

title.en: 'Fake gas shortage': Premier's fracking comments draw fury from conservationists

summary.en: Conservationists have criticized the Premier's comments on a gas shortage, arguing that Western Australia's issue is not a lack of supply but rather excessive gas exports.

body.en:
Talk of future gas fracking in a pristine wilderness area to bolster energy supply has sparked fresh fury from conservation groups.

Premier Roger Cook said Western Australia could be forced to permit fracking in the Kimberley region if Woodside Energy's $30 billion offshore Browse project was not developed and the state was left short of gas.

Cook told the Australian Financial Review that WA had a large deficit in its future energy needs, and renewable sources would not be able to replace the gas needed to meet demands from households and heavy industry.

His comments triggered an avalanche of criticism from environmental groups, with about 150 protesters rallying at WA parliament on Friday.

"The WA gas industry has manufactured a fake gas shortage by not supplying their own requisite 15 per cent of domestic gas to the WA market," Greenpeace's Geoff Brice told reporters.

"That is simply not good enough, and they use that to then justify opening up massive new gas expansions in places like the Kimberley and Scott Reef."

The Conservation Council said WA was not facing a gas supply problem, but it did have a gas export problem.

Playing off Woodside's Browse project against fracking in the Kimberley as an either-or scenario was disingenuous and misleading, the council said.

"Gas companies are meant to reserve 15 per cent of their gas for the domestic market, but deliver little more than half of that," executive director Matt Roberts said.

He also raised concerns about the impact Cook's remarks could have on the WA environmental watchdog.

"To have this public pressure mounted and political pressure mounted on the (WA Environmental Protection Authority), I find that unacceptable," he said.

"To think about drilling 50 oil and gas wells around Scott Reef and if that does not happen to frack the Kimberley, we cannot believe that the premier has said this," executive director Martin Pritchard said.

The Chamber of Minerals and Energy said WA would need significantly more gas in the coming years.

"If WA wants to maintain its standard of living ... and Australia wants to be relevant and safe in a more contested world, then it must develop its natural resources," chief executive Aaron Morey said.

"As we've learned through this period of the current global energy crunch, it is our energy resources that have put us in a position to ensure we attract the fuel and other resources we need to stay secure."

The WA domestic gas reservation scheme was a successful policy despite the differences of opinion about how much should be supplied, he said.

The WA Opposition energy spokesperson Steve Thomas said a more pressing issue was the capacity of the Dampier to Bunbury gas pipeline.

title.en: 'Has that been written off?': Fresh questions over Belle Gibson's $410,000 fine
title.zh: “这已经被注销了吗？”：关于 Belle Gibson 410,000 美元罚款的新问题

summary.en: The questions come after Premier Jacinta Allan said the consumer watchdog was "constantly and consistently" pursuing the fine.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Consumer Affairs Victoria has confirmed disgraced wellness influencer Belle Gibson's unpaid $410,000 court penalty has not been written off, with the state consumer watchdog saying it will continue to pursue the debt nearly a decade after the Federal Court ruling.

The clarification came during a parliamentary estimates hearing on Friday, after Victorian Nationals MP Jade Benham questioned officials about the status of the long-outstanding penalty and whether it had effectively been abandoned as bad debt.

Benham referenced comments made by Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan last year that Consumer Affairs Victoria was "constantly and consistently" pursuing Gibson over the fine, imposed in 2017 after she admitted lying about having terminal brain cancer and misleading consumers.

"I don't have any information that says that has been written off," Victoria's Consumer Affairs Minister Paul Edbrooke told the hearing before referring the question to Consumer Affairs Victoria director Nicole Rich.

"Ms Benham, we will continue to pursue that. It's a court penalty, so it will continue to be owed."

A Consumer Affairs Victoria spokesperson told SBS News the watchdog "has continued to undertake actions" to enforce the debt owed by Gibson under court order.

Gibson was ordered by the Federal Court in 2017 to pay $410,000 after Consumer Affairs Victoria successfully sued her for misleading and deceptive conduct over false claims she had terminal brain cancer and other cancers and had cured them through diet and alternative therapies.

She had also falsely claimed profits from her wellness brand, app and cookbook business would be donated to charity.

Interest and penalties later pushed the amount owed beyond $500,000, while authorities previously raided Gibson's Northcote home in attempts to seize assets.

The case returned to public attention last year, following the release of Netflix drama Apple Cider Vinegar, which dramatised Gibson's rise and fall and renewed scrutiny on whether the debt would ever be recovered.

Allan said in February that Consumer Affairs Victoria "won’t let up" in pursuing the outstanding penalty.

body.zh: 维多利亚州消费者事务部已证实，名誉扫地的健康影响者贝尔·吉布森 (Belle Gibson) 未付的 41 万澳元法庭罚款尚未被注销，该州消费者监管机构表示，在联邦法院裁决近十年后，将继续追究这笔债务。 这一澄清是在周五的议会预算听证会上做出的，此前维多利亚州国民议员杰德·贝纳姆 (Jade Benham) 向官员询问了长期未清罚金的状况，以及该罚金是否实际上已被视为坏账而被放弃。 Benham 引用了维多利亚州州长杰辛塔·艾伦 (Jacinta Allan) 去年发表的评论，称维多利亚州消费者事务部正在“持续不断地”追究吉布森的罚款，该罚款是在吉布森承认谎称患有晚期脑癌并误导消费者后于 2017 年处以的。 维多利亚州消费者事务部长保罗·埃德布鲁克（Paul Edbrooke）在听证会上表示：“我没有任何信息表明该费用已被注销，”然后将该问题转交给维多利亚州消费者事务部主任妮可·里奇（Nicole Rich）。 “贝纳姆女士，我们将继续追究这一点。这是法庭的处罚，所以将继续被欠。” 维多利亚州消费者事务部发言人告诉 SBS 新闻，监管机构“继续采取行动”，根据法院命令强制执行吉布森所欠的债务。 2017年，维多利亚州消费者事务部成功起诉吉布森，称她患有晚期脑癌和其他癌症，并通过饮食和替代疗法治愈了这些癌症，该事实具有误导性和欺骗性行为，联邦法院命令吉布森支付41万澳元。 她还谎称其健康品牌、应用程序和食谱业务的利润将捐赠给慈善机构。 后来利息和罚款使所欠金额超过了 50 万美元，而当局此前突击搜查了吉布森在诺斯科特的家，试图没收资产。 去年，Netflix 电视剧《苹果醋》上映后，该案重新受到公众关注，该剧戏剧化地讲述了吉布森的兴衰，并重新审视了债务能否收回的问题。 艾伦二月份表示，维州消费者事务部“不会放松”追究未缴罚款的责任。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。
